summary: The strongest opening is retatrutide for sleep apnea. NEJM published the TRIUMPH-1-OSA and TRIUMPH-2-OSA results on Oct 20, 2026, alongside the Sleep Europe presentation, and medical trade sites were still covering it on Oct 21–23. Two playbook patterns back it: next-gen explainers with the drug named first get a median of 44 long-form views, and retatrutide-named Shorts get a median of 120. It's about 3 days old, just past the 48-hour Lane C window, so publish it as a Lane C long-form only if it can go out today or tomorrow; otherwise make it a Lane A titled "Retatrutide for Sleep Apnea". Second is a gray-market piece. A JAMA Network Open paper (Oct 21) from Penn analysed about 150,000 Reddit posts on unapproved retatrutide, and CBS News reported on Oct 21 that its lab test of retatrutide it bought online was "pretty terrifying". That fits Lane B and the "honest uncertainty" format. Third is ACOG's first guidance on GLP-1s around pregnancy and breastfeeding (Healio, Oct 23), a fresh hook for a search-question long-form. It needs careful wording: report ACOG's advice, not ours. Fourth is an honest-uncertainty Short on semaglutide and the "eye stroke" (NAION), following our best-ever Reel. Evergreen Lane A topics stay strong: tirzepatide side effects (now in 6 snapshots), Wegovy pill vs shot (new uptake data), what happens when you stop, and Thanksgiving on GLP-1 (seasonal). Rejected: retatrutide sourcing and 'quality-control' checklists, and anything about telehealth shortcuts. Not used: the genetics story (it repeats an April 2026 Nature study), the Wegovy subscription (launched in March) and the mouse lifespan study (animal data only).

candidates.topic: Retatrutide for sleep apnea: TRIUMPH-1-OSA and TRIUMPH-2-OSA in NEJM (Oct 20, 2026). Adults with moderate-to-severe sleep apnea and obesity or overweight, with and without type 2 diabetes, 80 weeks
candidates.angle: New GLP-1 Drug Decoded: what changed for breathing at night, not just weight. Placebo-adjusted drops in breathing events per hour were about 22–24 without diabetes and about 14–15 with type 2 diabetes. 39–52% reached remission or mild disease without daytime sleepiness. Main side effects were stomach-related. Retatrutide is investigational, not approved. Give the tirzepatide sleep apnea approval as context, with no 'beat' framing.
candidates.predicted_peak: 2–10 days (trade press now; consumer and creator pickup next, plus Lilly Q3 results on Oct 29)
candidates.why_now: NEJM full results came out Oct 20, and Physicians Weekly, Medical Dialogues and MedPage covered them Oct 21–23. Retatrutide is our best-performing Shorts name (median 120). Few consumer YouTube explainers cover the sleep apnea trials yet. Lane C fits if it publishes immediately; otherwise use a search-led Lane A title. Title: 'Retatrutide for Sleep Apnea: What the New Trials Found'.

evidence.signal: Summary of the NEJM Oct 20 publication: 691 participants, 80 weeks, placebo-adjusted AHI reductions, 39–52% remission or mild disease
Retatrutide Once Weekly for Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea, the primary source
Lilly topline: AHI down by up to 36.1 events per hour (60.6%) from a baseline of 58.6

candidates.topic: Retatrutide bought online: what a JAMA Network Open Reddit study (Oct 21, 2026) and a CBS News lab test (Oct 21) found
candidates.angle: What's Actually Confirmed? Gray-market retatrutide is not the medicine in Lilly's trials. Penn researchers analysed about 150,000 Reddit posts from about 40,000 users. The most common classifiable report was increased appetite, the opposite of what the drug is designed to do, and the authors say this does not prove new side effects because nobody knows what is in the vials. Pair it with CBS's finding that vials were sold without any consultation and failed lab testing. Never name a seller. Point viewers to a prescriber about approved options or clinical trials.
candidates.why_now: Two independent sources in the same 48 hours: a peer-reviewed JAMA Network Open paper picked up by ScienceDaily, and a CBS News investigation. Many Google News results are search-query pages about retatrutide status and FDA concerns, which suggests heavy search demand. Gray-market 'what's confirmed' Shorts have a median of 106. Lane B long-form title: 'Retatrutide Online: What a New Study and Lab Tests Found'.

evidence.signal: About 150,000 Reddit posts; increased appetite most reported; more mentions of sleep, heart-rate and muscle symptoms; authors caution against reading these as proven side effects
Reporter bought 'retatrutide' online and at a bodega without a consultation; lab results called 'pretty terrifying'

candidates.topic: ACOG's first guidance on GLP-1 medicines, pregnancy and breastfeeding (Oct 23, 2026)
candidates.angle: Life on GLP-1 / search question: 'GLP-1 and pregnancy: what the OB-GYNs now recommend.' Report exactly what ACOG says: plan with your clinician 1–2 months before trying to conceive, and if the medicine is used while breastfeeding, the baby's weight gain is monitored. Explain why: long half-lives and limited data. Add context: no clear rise in birth defects after early accidental exposure (consensus), and the MHRA's advice. Present it only as 'what ACOG advises', and say to plan any change with your prescriber, never on your own.
candidates.predicted_peak: 2–6 days for news; then evergreen search
candidates.why_now: ACOG issued the guidance Oct 23 (Healio, The Independent), and the WSJ ran a breastfeeding piece the same day. It's high-intent search for women of reproductive age, a large part of our audience. Few creators have covered it yet.

evidence.signal: ACOG issues 'long-awaited' guidance: stop 1–2 months before pregnancy; monitor infant weight gain if used while breastfeeding
Consensus guidelines: don't deliberately continue in pregnancy; no increased congenital anomalies after early inadvertent exposure

candidates.topic: Semaglutide and 'eye stroke' (NAION): why Wegovy shows a stronger link than Ozempic, and what the absolute risk really is
candidates.angle: Honest uncertainty, following our best Reel: 'Semaglutide and Eye Stroke: What the Studies Can and Can't Say.' Say the worry is understandable. The studies are observational and the absolute risk is 'very, very low' (Academy 2026 speaker, Oct 2026). Explain why the Wegovy-versus-Ozempic difference may reflect who takes each and at what dose. Say what symptoms to report to a clinician promptly. No scare framing.
candidates.why_now: The Medical Economics Oct 23 roundup repeated the 'Wegovy may pose higher risk' headline, and two new cohorts are out (Clin Ophthalmol Oct 12; Cureus Oct 19, semaglutide vs tirzepatide). The macular degeneration honest-uncertainty Short got 105 on YouTube and 160 on Instagram.

evidence.signal: GLP-1s may be linked to vision loss, but overall risk 'very, very low'

candidates.topic: Semaglutide and alcohol: Heineken warns that weight-loss drugs may cut beer sales (Reuters and Guardian, Oct 23) while a 2026 RCT showed fewer heavy-drinking days
candidates.angle: 'Does Semaglutide Reduce Alcohol Cravings?' In the 2026 RCT (108 adults with alcohol use disorder and obesity, 26 weeks, alongside CBT), semaglutide cut heavy-drinking days by about 13.7 percentage points more than placebo. Explain the brain-reward mechanism. Semaglutide is not approved for alcohol use disorder; note STAT's report that telehealth is prescribing off-label for addiction.
candidates.why_now: Heineken's internal document (Reuters exclusive, Guardian, BeverageDaily) is a mainstream hook the same week as STAT's off-label addiction story. Strong US/UK audience fit.

evidence.signal: RCT: semaglutide 26 weeks with CBT reduced heavy-drinking days by an estimated 13.7 percentage points more than placebo

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines and blood pressure: meta-regression of 32 phase 3 trials (EClinicalMedicine, Oct 12) in about 43,600 adults with overweight or obesity
candidates.angle: 'Does Tirzepatide Lower Blood Pressure?' Across trials, systolic pressure fell about 5.2 mmHg placebo-adjusted. Weight loss explained about 77% of the variation, roughly 0.34 mmHg per 1% of weight lost. The medicine doesn't replace blood pressure drugs, and nobody should change their medication on their own.
